pages.text: An Electrode Holder only takes power through its $(item)top face$(). Run your cable to the top of each holder.

$(l)Current, not just voltage$()$(br)A holder works only when at least $(item)5 A$() flows through it (the server setting electrolysisMinimumCurrent, 5 by default). Current is voltage divided by resistance, and copper and zinc electrodes are $(item)10 ohm$() each:
$(li)$(item)50 V$() gives exactly 5 A, the minimum,$(li)below 50 V the holder idles and its multimeter line says not enough current.

$(l)Do not overdo it$()$(br)A holder breaks if it sees more than $(item)400 A$() or more than $(item)20000 V$() for a moment. With a 10 ohm electrode, 400 A is reached at $(item)4000 V$(), so keep copper and zinc holders well under that.
An empty holder has no resistance and draws nothing. Remember the vat rule: a holder with an electrode but not enough current blocks every recipe in that vat, not only electrolysis.
